text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- The Pila-based Philips Lighting plant has opened an environment-friendly oxygen generation facility at a cost of $5 million.
- Several hundred retail outlets and wholesalers around Poland have joined the Handel 2000 network, which will compete with the foreign supermarket chains.
Initially, Handel 2000 will set up around 20 regional centres throughout Poland.
- About 140 Polish firms want to participate in the seventh edition of the "Teraz Polska" quality contest of Polish-made products.
- Around 120 firms will exhibit products of over 300 producers at the Elektro Expo'96 electrical engineering international fair to take place in November in Warsaw.
- Granting Poland's farming sector entry to the EU may benefit European producers if they invest in the Polish food processing industry, the FAPA agricultural assistance foundation said.
- The Komfort household furnishings retail chain has recently opened its fifty-fifth shop in Gdynia, northern Poland, at a cost of $1 million.

- Gdynia shipyard should start generating profits in 1997 for the first time in several years and will join a larger shipyard holding which is currently in its planning stages, company management said.
- The National Bank of Poland (NBP), the central bank, has licensed Korea's LG Group to take over the new share issue of the Lodz-based Petrobank.
- Bank Pekao SA's net profit in the first three quarters of 1996 was at 201.8 million zlotys, representing 67.7 percent of last year's annual profit.
- By year-end the Gdynia port will reload up to 30,000 tonnes of imported Siberian coal contracted by three importers in northern Poland.
The port authorities expect a further reloading increase of coal imported from Australia, North America and Indonesia.
NOWA EUROPA
- Poland's government and the agricultural market regulator (ARR) will buy surplus sugar produce but will not subsidise its export and domestic sales

- Electricity consumers in urban and rural areas will pay the same prices due to the government's withdrawal from its previous programme of regionalised energy pricing, deputy industry minister Henryk Gabrys said.
- The Legnica-based Legmet mining machinery maker was granted an International Standards Organisation (ISO) 9001 certificate.

- Despite intensive advertising campaigns Poland's annual coffee consumption remains at the level of two kg per head, blocking future coffee industry investment, Prima coffee maker president Tomasz Szymczak said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- Following the start of a new speaker production line by the listed Tonsil sound equipment maker in spring next year the firm will apply for an ISO qulity certificate, company deputy president Andrzej Nowaczyk said.

- The U.S. Ameritech telecom company will sell its stake in the Centertel analogue mobile phone firm to the remaining stakeholders state-owned telecom monopolist Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA) and France Telecom.
ZYCIE
- A Polish-American joint venture will invest $47 million in the plasma processing plant located in the Mielec special economic zone in southeastern Poland.
- Seven municipalities in the Katowice province will issue municipal bonds to finance local modernisation and educational projects.
PARKIET
- The listed Novita carpet maker's net profit in 1996 will reach 4.2 million zlotys on revenues of 69 million zlotys, Novita President Marek Gorny said.
